front_question: What historical factor led to the rise of the consumer movement in India during the 1960s?
back_answer: Widespread consumer discontent regarding food shortages, hoarding, black marketing, under-weighing, and adulteration of food grains and edible oils.

front_question: What is COPRA, and when is National Consumers Day celebrated in India?
back_answer: Consumer Protection Act enacted in 1986 (updated 2019). National Consumers Day is celebrated every year on December 24.

front_question: List the six statutory Consumer Rights granted under COPRA.
back_answer: 1. Right to Safety, 2. Right to Information, 3. Right to Choose, 4. Right to be Heard / Representation, 5. Right to Seek Redressal, 6. Right to Consumer Education.

front_question: How does the Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005 empower citizens in relation to both market products and government services?
back_answer: For goods: Mandates package disclosures (ingredients, MRP, batch, expiry). For government: Enables citizens to demand official records on public work delays, administrative decisions, and public utility operations.

front_question: Name the three-tier quasi-judicial redressal commission structure established under COPRA and their 2019 monetary claim thresholds.
back_answer: 1. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (claims up to ₹1 crore). 2. State Consumer Commission (claims ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore). 3. National Consumer Commission (claims above ₹10 crore).

front_question: Identify the official quality certification marks for electrical goods, agricultural produce, and gold jewelry in India.
back_answer: Electrical/industrial goods: ISI Mark (BIS). Agricultural produce: Agmark. Gold jewelry: Hallmark (BIS).

front_question: Why is insisting on a cash receipt/bill critical when making consumer purchases?
back_answer: A cash receipt acts as legal documentary proof of purchase required by Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions to file claims for replacement or compensation.
